senses.definition: Covering a wide range of cases or topics rather than a narrow one.
senses.caution: A broad remit can sound unfocused, so name the few areas that matter most. As a noun it is old, offensive slang for a woman.
senses.example: The new team has a broad remit, from data quality to vendor contracts.

cues.text: A steering committee asks about the new team's remit. It reaches into every business unit rather than one specialism, and you want a word for how wide that is.
A friend asks what a mutual acquaintance is actually good at. She does many things capably rather than one thing brilliantly, and you mean that as praise.
You are choosing a film for a group with very different tastes and want a word for something with wide appeal rather than something you personally love.

distractors: Built for one customer rather than taken off the shelf.
Lasting only a short time, and meant to.
Safe to run more than once, because a repeat run changes nothing.
Present only in scattered places instead of everywhere across the organisation.
Using far more words than the point actually needs, in speech or on the page.

senses.definition: In general terms, true of most of it but without every detail or every person.
senses.caution: 'We broadly agree' tells people there is some disagreement, so expect to be asked where. Use it to be honest about gaps, and then name them.
senses.example: We broadly agree with the audit findings, but we would challenge the timeline on the second one.

cues.text: Your sponsor asks whether the other directors are behind the platform plan. Most are, one is not, and you want an honest word without opening that up now.
A director asks for the shape of next year's roadmap. You can give the outline but not the specifics, and you want to signal that as you start.
A friend asks whether you liked the book. You did overall, though two chapters dragged.

distractors: Exactly and in full, with every detail checked.
In secret, so that the people affected do not find out.
Only for a short time, until a proper plan has been agreed.
Against the advice of the people who know the subject best, and without telling them.
In the order that things happened, starting with the earliest event and ending with the latest.
